mutation: Seven mutations against the equivalence harness. G1: the expiry comparison inside the shared verifier was shifted an hour earlier. G2: the tenant resolver was given its own session resolution instead of calling the shared verifier. G3: a token shorter than eight characters was accepted as a forged identity. G4: `selectOrganisation`'s membership test was replaced with `if (true)`, so a preference naming an organisation the account never joined is trusted. G5: the switch adapter was given its own cookie-reading session resolution in place of `resolveServerSession`. G6: a submitted `accountId` was allowed to override the resolved one. G7a: `requireSession` was made to admit an `expired` verdict. G7b: `resolveServerSession` was made to read `getAll(SESSION_COOKIE)[0]`, taking the first duplicate cookie while every other path takes the last.
performedBy: executed during obligation 3, each mutation applied to the production source, measured, and reverted. G1 turned 'the expiry boundary is identical across entry points' false. G2 turned three tests false including the vector table. G3 turned the vector table and the duplicate-cookie test false. G6 turned 'no entry point derives identity from submitted fields' false. G4, G7a and G7b initially produced NO failure and that is the finding, twice over. G4 was absorbed: `resolveTenant` validates a preference through `selectOrganisation` and again through `governingMembership`, so weakening one leaves the other's refusal standing and an outcome-only harness reports the surviving check's answer as though both were intact — the same two-mechanism problem obligation 2 met in F3. The harness now asks the rule directly and compares its answer with the resolved one, and G4 fails as a disagreement. G7a was unreachable rather than absorbed: nothing under packages/ may import apps/web, so the two framework entry points are absent from the behavioural vector table entirely. The structural guard was extended to assert that neither entry point makes its refusal conditional on which refusal it is, and that neither selects among duplicate session cookies itself; with those, both mutations fail. All seven now bite. CORRECTION, made during obligation 4 on stronger evidence: G7b was described here as a second demonstration of architectural unreachability, and it was not. Obligation 4 ran the same mutation against a live development server and it again changed nothing, which prompted a direct check of the parser: `new RequestCookies(headers)` over a `Cookie` header carrying the same name twice reports `size` 1 and `getAll(name)` returns a single value — the last. Duplicates are collapsed into a Map before any application code can look, so `getAll(name)[0]` IS `get(name)` and the mutation was semantically inert rather than merely unobserved. The consequence is stronger than what obligation 3 claimed: no application code can select a different duplicate, because by the time it runs there is only one value to select. G7a's finding stands unchanged — that mutation is real and genuinely out of behavioural reach from `packages/`, which is why the structural guard and its recorded limitation remain.
